text:
maya: Heads-up — incoming escalation from a customer after today's canary. They say some responses reverted to an old onboarding template for a subset of requests. Repro steps and example attached.

devin: Can you paste the exact request payload + any request_id from their logs? :eyes:

maya: Here’s the payload they used (redacted tenant id):
```json
{
  "model": "redwood-qa/v2",
  "input": "Explain signup flow in 1 paragraph",
  "tenant_id": "tenant-REDACTED"
}
```
They attached a response that contains the old template header: "Welcome to Acme — get started by..." which shouldn't exist in v2.

devin: Searching logs for request_id: found several entries. Notable snippet: 
```
[2025-11-02T14:53:10Z] req=abcd1234 tenant=tenant-REDACTED model=redwood-qa/v2 cache_hit=true cache_key="resp:tenant-REDACTED:model:redwood-qa/v1:hash:0x3a7f"
[2025-11-02T14:53:10Z] req=abcd1234 response_template=onboarding_v1
```
Looks like the cache_key contains v1 but the request says v2 — possible key-versioning mismatch.

ops-bot: Canary rollout for redwood-qa/v2 started at 2025-11-02T14:30:00Z, 25% traffic.

ashok: If the cache key namespace doesn't include a model-version component (or that component changed format), older entries can shadow new outputs — "cache shadowing". That would explain only a subset of requests returning v1 content.

maya: Customer reports ~12% of their calls in the last hour affected, scattered across endpoints. Suspect per-tenant cache collisions due to key format change.

devin: Quick mitigation: flush tenant-specific response cache or bump namespace. Command to run on the infra cluster: 
```bash
# flush response cache for affected tenant
redwood cache delete --namespace tenant-REDACTED --pattern 'resp:*' --confirm
```
This will clear cached responses without touching other cache layers.

ashok: Longer-term fix: enforce versioned cache keys that include full model id + build hash. I'll open a PR to add model_build_hash into the cache key derivation and add a migration to detect format changes.

maya: Starting targeted cache purge for tenant-REDACTED now. Also temporarily paused the canary traffic for this tenant.

ops-bot: Cache purge job finished at 2025-11-02T14:57:05Z, status=success.

maya: Customer confirmed after purge responses are correct for new requests. We'll keep monitoring for 24h and schedule a follow-up postmortem. Drafting customer note with apology and explanation. :thumbsup:

devin: Adding unit test to ensure cache key always includes model build id. Also adding a small alert when cache_hit responses contain mismatched model identifiers in logs.

ashok: TL;DR: root cause = cache-key namespace/format change during rollout -> shadowed older cached responses. Mitigation = tenant-scoped purge + revert canary for affected tenants; permanent = versioned keys + detection.

maya: Filed support ticket and pinned logs + purge job id. Will update the incident tracker.
